thread:
anya: Quick triage note: onboarding Gemma-6B-int4 hit a subtle quality delta on punctuation-heavy evals. Looks like a tokenizer overlay mismatch + minor rotary head-indexing quirk. summary below.
kevin: short numbers?
anya: local smoke (50 prompts): gemma-int4 ppl=10.9, fp16=10.2. token-diff rate ~0.5% concentrated on ellipses/em-dash clusters. kv-warmup shows extra logit drop for tokens 2..7.
rohan: sounds like packer ordering + overlay loader endianness. did you try swapping tokenizer overlay to a different loader?
anya: yes 1 tested gemma-tokenizer with our runtime overlay and gemma-tokenizer+alternate-loader. when using alternate-loader token ids match gold for 95% of repros.
kevin: try rotary_scale=1.0 and rotary_autotune=off to see if warmup amplification disappears. also dump first-12 token logits per-head.
anya: running now. command I used: ```./scripts/simple_repro.sh --model gemma-6b:int4 --prompts tests/punct.txt --dump=ids,trace --rotary_scale=1.0```
ci-bot: regression-suite/kv-warmup flake detected on candidate 1779998888, job 1779998890 queued.
rohan: if alternate-loader fixes ids then we have two levers: loader shim or revert packer endian change. loader shim may be acceptable short-term. but add serialization versioning to packer.
kevin: agree. also add a tiny cross-tokenizer test to CI so future packer changes fail fast.
anya: I pushed a tiny shim PR that normalizes overlay endianness at load time (PR #8391). with shim, ppl back to 10.3 on the 50-prompt set and token-diff drops to 0.03%. but still 0.05 ppl early-step gap vs fp16.
rohan: ok that residual looks like kernel head-indexing noise. I'll run a kernel-addressing sanity check and pin a canary node to reproduce.
ops-bot: scheduled canary run on node canary-9 for 2h retention.
kevin: good. plan: (1) land shim to unblock canaries (2) bisect kernel address change and fix packing spec (3) add serialization/version checks + cross-tokenizer CI.
anya: will attach artifacts and token diffs to RG ticket RG-1779998888. will update after canary. :thumbsup:
